record.gene/protein+organism: RMJ07785 (paper WIT identifier; gi 1500322), Methanococcus jannaschii
record.starting_question: Which archaeal gene supplies missing shikimate kinase activity when known bacterial/eukaryotic kinase sequences find no candidate?
record.actual_observations: The target genome has dispersed chorismate genes. In Aeropyrum pernix and Pyrococcus abyssi, an unknown GHMP-kinase-like gene lies immediately downstream of shikimate dehydrogenase. Its homologs occur in pathway-bearing archaea but not the pathway-lacking P. horikoshii comparison. A separate GHMP paralog, RMJ01903, tracks threonine-biosynthesis genes in other archaeal genomes.
record.annotation_consequence: A nonorthologous archaeal shikimate kinase candidate can be distinguished from the homoserine kinase paralog despite misleading sequence similarity.
record.experiment_dependence: Purified recombinant RMJ07785 phosphorylated shikimate; RMJ01903 phosphorylated homoserine. Cross-substrate assays detected no overlapping activity. These assays establish specificity beyond pathway association.
record.reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Reported sequence: no local clustering -> inspect other genomes; homoserine-like similarity conflicts with chorismate context -> compare the other GHMP paralog and both substrate panels. record.gene/protein+organism: BioY and BioMN, Rhodobacter capsulatus SB1003
record.starting_question: Must the BioY-associated biotin transporter always include the BioMN ATPase/membrane module?
record.actual_observations: Many bioY loci associate with biotin biosynthesis/regulons, but only approximately one-third link to bioMN; some genomes lack obvious BioMN homologs. record.annotation_consequence: PurT provides an alternative GAR-formylation route; effectiveness depends on substrate supply. It is not evidence that folate dependence of the entire purine pathway disappears.
record.experiment_dependence: Authors’ genetic and in-vitro formate-dependent activity experiments.

record.starting_question: Does a QueG annotation gap mean loss of mature queuosine, or another protein supplying the final reaction?

actual_observations.observation: Authors found inverse QueG/DUF208 distribution, Q-pathway neighborhoods and QueA fusions.
LC-MS detected Q in QueG-lacking L. salivarius grown in rich MRS.
A. baylyi single deletions retained Q; double ΔqueG Δduf208 accumulated oQ and lost Q.
Eight heterologous DUF208 genes restored Q in E. coli ΔqueG, with variable residual oQ.
Purification instability prevented in-vitro validation; limited recombinant-protein spectra did not detect cobalamin.
actual_observations.inspection_location: Cobalamin Seems Not to Be Associated; Conclusions

record.starting_question: Can ThyA alone replace ThyX in a bacterium without annotated FolA?

actual_observations.observation: thyX disruption caused thymidine auxotrophy. ThyA alone gave slow/incomplete rescue; ThyA plus FolA restored near-parent growth and more labeled dT synthesis.

record.annotation_consequence: Same desired dTMP output does not make the alternatives metabolically interchangeable: ThyA replacement imposes folate-recycling demand. No particular native backup reductase was identified.
record.experiment_dependence: Native gene disruption, controlled complementation and radioactive precursor incorporation.

record.starting_question: What does the unknown N-terminal domain fused to a newly identified NAD(P)HX-repair dehydratase contribute?
record.actual_observations: Yeast dehydratase YKL151C corresponds to YjeF’s C-terminal domain. YjeF’s N-terminal domain has separate yeast/mammalian homologs; fusion suggests related reactions. Known dehydratase stereoselectivity suggested an epimerase partner. Recombinant YjeF repairs both epimers. An ATP-regeneration system unexpectedly abolished bacterial activity, prompting ADP testing.
record.annotation_consequence: Bifunctional NAD(P)HX epimerase and ADP-dependent NAD(P)HX dehydratase; the cofactor cannot simply be transferred from the ATP-dependent eukaryotic homolog.
record.experiment_dependence: Fusion supports functional coupling, not epimerase chemistry. HPLC with enriched epimers, with/without ADP, and nucleotide measurements established epimerization, repair, and ADP-to-AMP coupling.
record.reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors explicitly infer the epimerase hypothesis from domain fusion plus an unprocessed epimer, then revise ATP to ADP after a contradictory assay result. This is reported reasoning, condensed here.
record.verification_scope: Complete main experimental procedures and relevant results read from full PMC HTML; supplementary procedures not independently inspected. No new sequence/fusion search or assays.
